title: IAHR-APD Annual Report 2025
summary: The Division's report to the IAHR Council for 2025.

body.text: Including but not limited to conferences, webinars, publications, working meetings, elections, participation in international processes, etc. Some examples below:
2025 IAHR-APD Executive Committee (EC) Meeting in Singapore
CHAIR: Norio Tanaka (IAHR-APD Chair), Won Kim (IAHR-APD Secretary)

items: Key Outcomes:
Marked the first fully face-to-face EC meeting since the pandemic, with strong attendance (10 out of 15 members, 67%).
Reviewed 2024–25 APD activities and financial reports.
Endorsed the host cities for the 25th and 26th Congresses.
Approved by-law amendments regarding the Executive Committee size, YPN seat, and Secretariat rules.
All proceedings were documented in the official minutes for transparency and archival purposes.

body.text: Continues joint publication (Elsevier) with KWRA & IAHR-APD.

items: Performance: Achieved a 2024 Impact Factor of 2.3, demonstrating a steady upward trend.
Editorial Standards: Maintained rigorous academic standards, with a 78% rejection rate during preliminary screening.
Process Improvements: Introduced a fast-track review system for leading scholars to accelerate review turnaround and enhance publication rates.
Strategic Goals: Set future objectives to promote research focusing on climate change, artificial intelligence (AI), and hydro-environmental sensing technologies.
Special Issues: Continued emphasis on publishing special issues to attract high-quality submissions.

25th IAHR-APD Congress – “Hydro-environments in the Era of Climate Change and AI”

items: Objective: To provide a collaborative platform for knowledge-sharing, exchange, and technological presentations in water science and engineering across the Asia-Pacific region.
Subthemes: Climate change, AI & water, fluvial processes, eco-hydraulics, urban hydrology, estuarine hydraulics, and more.

Organizing Body: Led by the Local Organizing Committee (LOC) comprising over 100 local experts, an International Advisory Committee, and an International Scientific Committee (ISC) with over 26 members.

Program Structure: Includes keynote speeches, technical sessions, welcome & closing ceremonies, and technical tours. Twelve special sessions have been proposed, with further proposals from EC members strongly encouraged.
Call to Action: Strong support and active participation from EC members are requested to ensure a successful event..

body.text: 26th IAHR-APD Congress – “He Tāonga te Wai – Water is a Treasure”

items: Tentative Date: February 8–12, 2028 (Strategically scheduled around the Lunar New Year and local holidays)
Venue: Rutherford House, Victoria University of Wellington (CBD, near the railway station), New Zealand
Progress & Strategy:
The Scientific Committee is currently being assembled, with a strong focus on encouraging regional collaboration.
Promotional activities will remain low-key until the conclusion of the 2026 Incheon Congress.
